newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh's Chittagong port strike ends.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh's Chittagong port strike ends.

text.p: The five-day-old strike in Bangladesh's main Chittagong port ended on Thursday with some 22,000 workers back at their jobs, port officials said.
They said the strike was withdrawn after Chittagong City Mayor A.B.M. Mohiuddin Chowdhury successfully brokered an agreement on Wednesday night between strikers and port users.
Users and the Chittagong Port Authority (CPA) signed the agreement following the meeting, port officials said.
"Normalcy has started returning at the port," CPA's Traffic Director Mohsin Sarkar told Reuters.
"But a fresh stalemate might surface any moment as different groups (workers, employees and users) are still pursuing selfish intentions," he added.
The strike began on Saturday as the workers walked out after Bangladeshi Q.C. Shipping Ltd began using its own cargo-handling equipment, permitted under the government's privatisation plan.
The workers and their Collective Bargaining Agent opposed the move and forced the CPA to withdraw the permission. But Q.C. Shipping later won a High Court verdict and overran the restrictions.

Wednesday's agreement envisaged that "the port users would cooperate with the CPA to make the port fully operative from Thursday morning. The port authority would withdraw the instructions and restrictions imposed on Q. C. Shipping."
The government, now reviewing the port situation in the wake of the strike, would come back soon with a "clear decision" on the use of private equipment, CPA officials said.
Some 25 ships have been stranded at the port since Saturday while 20 others were at the outer anchorage, port officials said.
